preconditions.expression: all(c in {'*', '#', '@'} for c in str1) and all(c in {'*', '#', '@'} for c in str2)
preconditions.description: Every character in str1 and str2 must be one of the three allowed tree categories: '*', '#', or '@'.
The lengths of str1 and str2 must be between 1 and 100, inclusive.

postconditions.expression: return_value == max(sum(str1[i] == str2[j] for i in range(len(str1)) for j in range(len(str2))) for _ in range(len(str1) + len(str2)))
postconditions.description: The function returns the maximum number of bridges that can be built, where each bridge connects a tree in str1 to a tree in str2 of the same category, and no two bridges share a tree from either side (i.e., each tree is used at most once).

postconditions.expression: return_value == len({(i, j) for i in range(len(str1)) for j in range(len(str2)) if str1[i] == str2[j] and all(i != i2 or j != j2 for (i2, j2) in {(i, j)}.union({(i, j) for i in range(len(str1)) for j in range(len(str2)) if str1[i] == str2[j] and i != i2 and j != j2}))})
postconditions.description: The returned value is the size of the maximum matching of trees between str1 and str2 where each matched pair has the same category, and no two pairs share a tree from either side.
